nodes.label: Necessity Witness Setup
nodes.statement: Fix nonempty Omega, total Boolean F and n>=1 total Boolean g_i; define Theta=AND_i g_i. Require jointly an admissible w* in Omega and j in {1,...,n} with F(w*)=1 and g_j(w*)=0. F interpretation is independent of Theta.

nodes.scope: Classical two-valued scoped domain; actual application additionally requires physical admissibility and independent target evidence.
nodes.proof: A one-element abstract domain with F=1 and g_1=0 is jointly satisfiable; not an actual phenomenal witness.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Report-only evidence does not establish F_O; undefined predicates require domain repair, not zero fill.

nodes.label: Relational Selection Setup
nodes.statement: Let K have one sort, constant a and unary f. D has carrier {0,1}, a=0, f(0)=1, f(1)=0; theta(x) is x=a and S={0}.
nodes.domain: One fully specified finite abstract K-structure.
nodes.scope: One fully specified finite abstract K-structure.
nodes.proof: All carrier, constant and function assignments are explicit and jointly satisfiable.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Not a human or experiential observation; arbitrary relational selectors of higher arity are tuple relations.

nodes.label: Selection Closure Limit
nodes.statement: Definability alone does not guarantee substructure closure: in RELATIONAL_SELECTION_SETUP, f(0)=1 is outside S. R157 formula transport remains valid for the selected relation; closure/physical autonomy are additional obligations.
nodes.domain: General not-guaranteed claim witnessed by one finite structure; closure means contains constants and closed under functions in a fixed signature.
nodes.scope: General not-guaranteed claim witnessed by one finite structure; closure means contains constants and closed under functions in a fixed signature.
nodes.proof: 0 belongs to S while its f-image does not; this refutes the general entailment. Isomorphism carries both selected set and function, preserving the failure.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Purely relational induced substructures may be available; an arbitrary tuple relation still is not itself a carrier. C1 is not refuted.
